original_question: What is the composition of gamma-ray-burst ejecta at the prompt-emission radius: are the outflows primarily matter-dominated fireballs or magnetically dominated jets, and what are the baryon, lepton-pair, and neutron contents of the flow? Here the key quantity is the magnetization sigma, the ratio of Poynting flux to matter flux, and the problem is to determine whether sigma is much less than 1, of order 1, or much greater than 1 in the emitting region.
target_in_paper: The distribution of energy between matter and magnetic fields is denoted by the magnetization factor σ (where the magnetic field and the matter density are measured in the lab frame), the ratio between Poynting flux and matter flux. Within the matter content, one has the baryonic and leptonic components, with the relative distribution denoted by a parameter f_e ≡ n_e/n_p. The abundance of free neutrons is usually denoted by the neutron-to-proton number ratio, ξ ≡ n_n/n_p. As a result, one needs to specify a radius (from the central engine) when judging whether the flow is matter-dominated (σ << 1) or magnetically-dominated (σ >> 1).
correct_elements: The draft correctly focuses on the ejecta composition question, identifying the magnetization parameter σ as the key measure distinguishing matter-dominated fireballs versus magnetically-dominated jets, and includes the roles of baryonic (proton), leptonic (electron/positron), and neutron components of the flow.
missing_details: Explicit definition of the magnetization parameter σ ≡ (Poynting flux)/(matter flux) measured in the lab frame.
Explicit definitions of the lepton-to-proton number ratio f_e ≡ n_e/n_p and the neutron-to-proton number ratio ξ ≡ n_n/n_p.
Specification of the prompt-emission radius R_em (above the photosphere) at which σ, f_e, and ξ are evaluated.
Clarification that heavy ion contamination is negligible, so baryonic content consists solely of protons and neutrons.
Acknowledgment that σ evolves with radius due to magnetic acceleration and dissipation, requiring evaluation of σ at R_em.
Context that the composition question applies to both massive star core collapse and compact star merger central engines.
refined_question: At the prompt-emission radius R_em (above the photosphere) of gamma-ray bursts, what is the magnetization parameter σ(R_em) ≡ (Poynting flux)/(matter flux), and what are the characteristic number ratios of leptons to protons f_e ≡ n_e/n_p and neutrons to protons ξ ≡ n_n/n_p? Specifically, do prompt GRB outflows satisfy σ(R_em) << 1 (matter-dominated fireballs), σ(R_em) ≃ 1 (quasi-magnetized flows), or σ(R_em) >> 1 (Poynting-flux-dominated jets), and what ranges of f_e and ξ best describe the ejecta composition at the emission site?
justification: Section 2.4 of the paper ('Ejecta Composition') defines the ejecta energy partition in terms of σ, f_e, and ξ and highlights the need to evaluate these parameters at a specified radius from the central engine. The refined question encapsulates the paper’s intent to diagnose whether GRB ejecta are matter- or magnetically-dominated at the prompt-emission radius and to quantify the baryonic and leptonic composition in terms of the defined parameters.
